title: 3-bet all-in with 15–25 BB
summary: The reshove: taking the dead money when a late position opens.

idea.text: With 15–25 BB, calling an open and playing out of position is unprofitable, and a normal 3-bet eats a third of your stack. The best tool is the **3-bet all-in** (a reshove): the opponent opens, you put it all in.

dead.text: Why it pays: the pot already holds **dead money**, the opener's raise, the blinds and the ante. Example: CO opens to 2.2 BB, you have 20 BB on the button. The pot is 2.2 + 0.5 + 1 + 1 (ante) = 4.7 BB. Every time CO folds, you win almost a quarter of your stack without a showdown.

range.caption: Button against a CO open, 20 BB: a simplified reshove range.

who.text:
The later the opener's seat, the wider the open and the more often it folds to an all-in. Against a CO or button open the reshove goes with 66+, A9s+, ATo+, KQ and also A5s–A4s (they block aces). Against an UTG open it is much tighter.

Hands that play well all-in are pairs and aces: they keep good equity even when called. Suited connectors like 87s are better as flat calls with deep stacks, not as reshoves.

q-aj.q: You have 18 BB on the button, CO opens to 2.2 BB. What is usually best with AJo?
q-aj.explain: AJo is strong against a CO open, plays well all-in, and calling leaves an awkward stack.

t1.q: What is the dead money in a reshove?
options: Chips in the pot you take when the opponent folds
t1.explain: The open, blinds and ante are already in: a fold hands them to you.

t2.q: Against whose open is the reshove wider?
options: It doesn’t depend on the seat
t2.explain: A late open is wider and folds more often.

t3.q: Which hands suit a reshove best?
t3.explain: They keep good equity when the opener calls.
